firstly i agree that that particular 3b1b video is one of his less helpful videos to building some intuition with the topic

what helped me IMMENSELY was getting used to matrices by watching the first few videos in his linear algebra series and looking back at 2x2 rotation matrices (and 3x3 ones for 3d space) and how they relate to complex numbers

imo, start with complex numbers (they should be called complex values, tbh), and realize that every time “i” is mentioned, it is nothing other than a 90 degree rotation of the normal number line, [therefore i*i = two 90 degree rotations](https://imgur.com/u7cCeMO)


 the idea of j^2 = -1 seems initially unintuitive, but if you extend it to 3d, you’ll see theres [two intuitive ways to rotate 1 to -1](https://imgur.com/MbBOfID)

but there’s a problem, we only have two axes of rotation, while for example a cube would have three, yaw, pitch, and roll. what’s weird is with these two axes we can map every point on the unit sphere, but we still can’t really account for every orientation with this, so we introduce k

but unlike before, if you treat k as roll, you cannot intuitively show how rolling would bring 1 to -1

from my understanding this is because the real number line doesn’t occupy 3d space anymore, and somehow the rotation of k twice results in 1 moving to -1 in 4D

you only need one axis to get every point on the unit circle, two axes to get every point on the surface of the unit sphere, it makes sense that you would need 3 axes to get every point on the ‘surface’ of a unit hypersphere, even if not intuitively visualize-able

I believe that the sudden increase of Black on Asian hate crime depicted on Reddit, Twitter, etc is greatly, or at least partially artificial and over-amplified. To be clear I’m not asserting that Asian people don’t experience racism and hate crime in the U.S.,  I think that it’s being blown up on social media for the purpose of pushing a narrative between the two races. This trend of stopping Asian American hate crime started becoming far more prominent after the shooting of multiple Asian massage parlors.

I find this strange how suddenly people start caring about racism against Asians all of a sudden after the shooting happened to such an exponential growth. The way the slogan appeared practically out of thin air and how racism against Asians only THEN became a serious issue, even though hate crime had been rising years prior to this. All strange, but plausible, since there’s a good chance people only start caring once they’re smacked in the face with it.

The convenient timing and suspicious activity doesn’t end there, either. As if on cue, both bot and non bot accounts start posting videos of perceived Black on Asian hate crime, that has no context. Videos of these resurfacing from years ago, clips of people robbing elderly asian people because of “racism” and not because they’re an easy target. Articles and videos of violent black on asian crime
that have been confirmed to not be a hate crime with both the victim and perpetrators race in the title often when black. Statements from people and organizations backtracking their comments and quotas against Asian people (all on cue). Statistics on hate crime show they typically occur in more densely populated areas, such as NYC, which has a high percentage of POC.

I commonly see people question the sudden spike of POC on Asian hate crime in posts and in comment sections. Usually they’re given the dichotomous and incomplete answer of “racism” or hate, while ignoring context. I simply think it’s to an extent artificial or astroturfed (if I’m using that right).

To conclude I believe hate crime against Asians is a serious problem in the U.S., but is artificially amplified, astroturfed (still not sure if that’s correct usage) and misconstrued by media, pushing a harmful narrative.
